title: Properties of the final descended model
statement:
For $Y\to S$ as in [def-nagata-final-descended-model], the morphism
$Y_{\lambda_Y}\to S_{\lambda_Y}$ is separated and of
finite presentation, $S_{\lambda_Y}$ is Noetherian, and $\epsilon_Y$ is an
isomorphism over $S$.

proof.text: By the definition of $Y_{\lambda_Y}$ and $\epsilon_Y$, apply [lemma-nagata-separated-eventually] to the separated finite-presentation morphism $Y\to S$. It gives that $Y_{\lambda_Y}\to S_{\lambda_Y}$ is separated and of finite presentation, and that its base change to $S$ is canonically $Y\to S$; under the defining notation this canonical comparison is the isomorphism $\epsilon_Y$.
The chosen stage $S_{\lambda_Y}$ is one of the stages in the final Noetherian base system, so [lemma-nagata-final-noetherian-base-system] says that it is Noetherian.
